protocol.name: xd_window_arranger_v1

description.summary: XeonDesktop: arrange windows from the taskbar

protocol.description: Private to XeonDesktop. The compositor only advertises this global to the shell process it started and to XeonDesktop's Task Manager (its Windows menu's Tile and Cascade). The shell uses it for the taskbar menu's Cascade Windows, Tile Windows Horizontally/Vertically and their Undo, for the window menu's Move and Size, for the language indicator (the keyboard layout), for Windows 7's taskbar thumbnails and Aero Peek, to hear of the lid and the power and sleep buttons, and for the virtual desktops' pager and the window menu's workspace items.

request.name: arrange

description.summary: arrange every visible window on each output

request.description: Arranges the windows that aren't minimized within each output's work area, remembering where they were for undo.

description.summary: put windows back where the last arrange found them

request.name: begin_move

description.summary: move the focused window with the keyboard

request.description: Starts keyboard move of the focused window, as the window menu's Move does: arrows (or the mouse) move it, Enter or a click keeps the new place, Esc puts it back. The shell activates the window first.

request.name: begin_size

description.summary: resize the focused window with the keyboard

request.description: Starts keyboard sizing of the focused window, as the window menu's Size does: the first arrow on each axis picks an edge, then arrows (or the mouse) move it; Enter or a click keeps it, Esc undoes it.

event.name: start_menu

description.summary: toggle the Start menu

event.description: Sent for the Windows key (pressed and released alone) and Ctrl+Esc: the shell opens the Start menu on this output, or closes it if open.

event.name: window_menu

description.summary: show the focused window's window menu

event.description: Sent for Alt+Space, a click on the caption icon, a right-click on the title bar, or a client's xdg_toplevel.show_window_menu. The window is already focused. x and y are output-local logical coordinates of the menu's top-left corner; serial is for the popup grab.

event.name: attention

description.summary: a window wants the user's attention

event.description: Sent when a window asked to be activated without the user's say-so (an xdg-activation token that didn't come from the focused app or the shell). The window isn't focused; the shell flashes its taskbar button until it's activated, as Windows does.

request.name: arrange_app

description.summary: arrange one program's windows

request.description: As arrange, but only the windows whose app id is app_id (a group button's Cascade and Tile); its minimized windows are restored first, as XP does.

request.name: mark

description.summary: add a window to the next arrange_marked

request.description: Task Manager's Windows menu arranges the windows selected on its Applications tab: it marks each (by its own foreign-toplevel handle), then asks for the arrangement.

request.name: arrange_marked

description.summary: arrange the marked windows

request.description: As arrange, but only the marked windows (minimized ones are restored first); the marks are cleared.

request.name: set_always_on_top

description.summary: keep one of the client's own windows above others

request.description: Task Manager's Options > Always On Top: the window (the client's own toplevel's surface) stays above ordinary windows, below the taskbar, until set back. Its dialogs come along.

request.name: peek

description.summary: Aero Peek: see through every window

request.description: While on, every window but its outline is transparent, so the desktop shows (the taskbar's Show desktop corner, hovered).

request.name: set_keyboard_layout

description.summary: switch the keyboard layout

request.description: The taskbar's language indicator: makes layout `index` (the XKB group, counted from 0 in [Keyboard] Layout's order) the active one on every keyboard, at once and for this session only, as the layout switching keys do. An index past the keymap's layouts is ignored.

event.name: keyboard_layout

description.summary: the active keyboard layout

event.description: Sent to the shell when it binds and whenever the active layout changes: by the switching keys, set_keyboard_layout, or a new keymap. index is the XKB group, counted from 0.

request.name: identify

description.summary: ask for a window's ext-foreign-toplevel-list identifier

request.description: The compositor answers with the identifier event if the window has an ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1, so the shell can capture it (ext-image-copy-capture-v1 through ext-foreign-toplevel-image-capture-source-v1) for its taskbar thumbnail. Those globals, like this one, are only offered to the shell the compositor started.

event.name: identifier

description.summary: a window's ext-foreign-toplevel-list identifier

event.description: The answer to identify: the identifier of the window's ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1.

request.name: peek_window

description.summary: Aero Peek at one window

request.description: A taskbar thumbnail hovered: every other window turns to its faint outline, as peek does, and this one shows in front of them. Null ends it. A minimized window isn't shown.

event.name: window_menu_keyboard

description.summary: the next window menu was asked for from the keyboard

event.description: Sent just before window_menu when Alt+Space asked for it, not the pointer: the menu underlines its access keys even when they're hidden until the keyboard is used, as Windows' menus do.

event.name: power_button

description.summary: the lid or a power button

event.description: Sent to the shell when the lid switch toggles and when the power or sleep button is pressed (those keys go to no window). The shell carries out Power Options' action for it while it holds logind's block inhibitor for that button; otherwise logind acts and the shell ignores the event.

request.name: test_lid

description.summary: testing only: as if the lid switch toggled

request.description: For UI tests on a headless compositor, which has no lid switch: the compositor acts as for the lid closing (closed nonzero) or opening. Ignored unless it runs with --allow-virtual-input, which also offers this global to every client.

event.name: session_locked

description.summary: the screen is locked, or unlocked

event.description: Sent to the shell when a session lock covers every monitor (the lock's frames have been shown on each, not only asked for), with locked nonzero, and when the session is unlocked, with zero; and when the shell binds while locked. The shell lets the computer sleep, or another user's session start, only once it's locked.

event.name: desktops

description.summary: the virtual desktops, and which one shows

event.description: Sent to the shell when it binds and whenever Desktop Effects' General Options change how many desktops there are, or another one is switched to. They are numbered from 0, row by row from the top left. With one (1 x 1, the default) there are none to speak of: the shell shows no pager and the window menu no workspace items. Only the windows on the current desktop, and those on every desktop, have foreign-toplevel handles, so the taskbar shows just those.

request.name: switch_desktop

description.summary: show another desktop

request.description: The pager: desktop `index` is shown, with the transition the effects turned on give it. Past the last one, ignored.

event.name: window_desktop

description.summary: the desktop a window is on

event.description: Sent for each window as it gets its foreign-toplevel handle, and when it's made sticky or not: the desktop it's on, and whether it shows on every desktop (the window menu's Always on Visible Workspace).

request.name: move_window_to_desktop

description.summary: the window menu's Move to Another Workspace

request.description: The window (and its dialogs) goes to desktop `index`, which isn't switched to; a sticky window stops being sticky.

request.name: set_window_sticky

description.summary: the window menu's Always on Visible Workspace

request.description: Nonzero: the window shows on every desktop; zero: only on the current one.
